newsitem.title: JAPAN: Top execs not involved in scandal - Nomura's ex-head.
newsitem.headline: Top execs not involved in scandal - Nomura's ex-head.

text.p: Former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki said on Friday that he believed no other senior executives of the company were involved in a scandal over suspected illegal payments.

"I had a report (from our in-house investigation) that no (more) senior executives were involved in the case and I believe that no senior executives were involved in it," he told a parliamentary committee that is looking into the scandal over payments to a client linked to corporate racketeers, or sokaiya.
Nomura has said that two of its directors were involved in the apparently illegal deals, in which profits were funnelled to the sokaiya-linked client.
Sakamaki resigned as Nomura president in mid-March to take managerial responsibility for the scandal, becoming an adviser to the company.
On March 6, Nomura said an internal probe had found that the two directors had transferred money from a Nomura account to a corporate client's account.

A few days later, the two Nomura directors resigned after the internal probe found they made discretionary deals banned under Japanese securities law and funnelled profits to a front company for sokaiya.
Prosecutors and officials from Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), raided Nomura on March 25 looking for evidence in the case.
"Sokaiya" extort money from a company by threatening to disturb a shareholders' meeting, or offering to prevent a disruption of the proceedings by unruly shareholders.
Japanese commercial law has prohibited paying off racketeers since 1982.
